hints: Set up the area integral $\int_0^4 \left[ (2x^{1/2} + 1) - \left(\frac{1}{2}x^2 - x + 1\right) \right] dx$.
walkthrough:
Set up the definite integral for the area bounded between the two curves from $x = 0$ to $x = 4$:
$$\text{Area} = \int_0^4 \left[ (2x^{1/2} + 1) - \left(\frac{1}{2}x^2 - x + 1\right) \right] dx = \int_0^4 \left( 2x^{1/2} - \frac{1}{2}x^2 + x \right) dx$$

Integrate each term with respect to $x$:
$$\int 2x^{1/2} dx = \frac{2x^{3/2}}{3/2} = \frac{4}{3}x^{3/2}, \quad \int -\frac{1}{2}x^2 dx = -\frac{1}{6}x^3, \quad \int x dx = \frac{1}{2}x^2$$
$$\text{Area} = \left[ \frac{4}{3}x^{3/2} - \frac{1}{6}x^3 + \frac{1}{2}x^2 \right]_0^4$$

hints: Differentiate both curve equations to find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at $x = 4$.
Find the gradient of the upper curve $m_1 = x^{-1/2} = \frac{1}{2}$ and lower curve $m_2 = x - 1 = 3$.
Calculate the angle of inclination of each tangent line using $\tan^{-1}(m)$ and subtract to find $\alpha$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate both curves with respect to $x$:
$$\text{Upper curve: } y = 2x^{1/2} + 1 \implies \frac{dy}{dx} = x^{-1/2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}$$
$$\text{Lower curve: } y = \frac{1}{2}x^2 - x + 1 \implies \frac{dy}{dx} = x - 1$$

Evaluate the gradients of both tangents at the intersection point $B(4, 5)$:
$$m_1 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{4}} = \frac{1}{2} = 0.5$$
$$m_2 = 4 - 1 = 3$$

Calculate the angles of inclination of the tangents with the horizontal:
$$\theta_1 = \tan^{-1}(0.5) \approx 26.565^\circ$$
$$\theta_2 = \tan^{-1}(3) \approx 71.565^\circ$$

Calculate the angle $\alpha$ between the two tangent lines:
$$\alpha = \theta_2 - \theta_1 = 71.565^\circ - 26.565^\circ = 45^\circ$$
